# rc-mcp

> Personal fleet remote-control system built on the Model Context Protocol
> (MCP). Lets an MCP-capable LLM client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or any
> spec-compliant host) inspect and control your own Linux desktop machines:
> shell, filesystem, processes, screenshots, sysinfo, and (opt-in) input
> injection.

Single-operator tool, not a multi-tenant service: no user management or
RBAC. The security model keeps the LLM client from doing anything the
operator didn't approve in the moment, not from isolating users from each
other.

Two binaries, one Go module (`github.com/champi-ai/rc-mcp`, Go 1.25+):

- `rc-mcp-server` (`cmd/server`) — relay hub. Speaks MCP over Streamable
  HTTP to LLM clients and a WebSocket wire protocol to agents; routes tool
  calls between them; never executes tool logic itself. Also serves a
  loopback-only admin API/web UI for pairing.
- `rc-mcp-agent` (`cmd/agent`) — runs on each controlled machine. Dials out
  to the server (no inbound port needed), and does the actual work.

Everything that mutates state requires live MCP elicitation confirmation
from the human at the client before dispatch; every call is audited.

## Core docs

- [README.md](README.md): project overview, quick start (run server, pair
  a machine, point an MCP client at it), configuration env vars, security
  model.
- [docs/specs/backend.md](docs/specs/backend.md): the full protocol, wire
  format, and architecture specification — authoritative source for tool
  schemas, message types, and config.

## Installation

- [docs/guides/install-server.md](docs/guides/install-server.md): three
  ways to run the server — Docker Compose (with nginx/TLS), a published
  Docker image, or a from-source systemd service.
- [docs/guides/install-agent.md](docs/guides/install-agent.md): installing
  the agent on a controlled machine as a systemd user service, config,
  and pairing it with the server.
- [docs/examples/mcp-config.json](docs/examples/mcp-config.json): example
  `mcpServers` JSON config for pointing Claude Desktop/Claude Code at the
  server.

## Operations

- [docs/operations/releases.md](docs/operations/releases.md): how the
  agent and server components are versioned and released (release-please
  on merge to main, or manual tag push).
- [docs/operations/agent-releases.md](docs/operations/agent-releases.md):
  agent binary release/download URLs and the auto-update mechanism.
- [docs/operations/server-releases.md](docs/operations/server-releases.md):
  server Docker image release and deploy.
- [docs/operations/scaling.md](docs/operations/scaling.md): running more
  than one server replica with Redis-backed session/device state.

## Design history

- [docs/adr/](docs/adr/): architecture decision records (e.g. why Nx was
  tried for CI orchestration, then dropped — see ADR 0001, superseded).
- [docs/phases/](docs/phases/): how the MVP and post-MVP work was
  sequenced.
- [docs/review/senior-review.md](docs/review/senior-review.md): senior
  review notes on the spec before implementation began.

## Optional

- [.env.example](.env.example): every configuration environment variable
  with its default.
- [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml) /
  [docker-compose.scaling.yml](docker-compose.scaling.yml): local and
  multi-replica deployment topology.
